transcript: One of the many things that made the RENT 30th anniversary concert last night so special is that typically with these reunion concerts, they're pretty exclusive. They're usually in New York, one night only, with tickets going for a lot of money, if you can even get them. And while all of those things were also true for RENT, they also had a live stream option where you could watch it from your home anywhere in the U S For only $30, making it way more accessible than any of the reunion concerts that have come before it. And accessibility has always been such a core part of Rent's identity. RENT was actually the first Broadway show to ever have a rush policy, selling the first two rows of the theatre day of for only $20, because Jonathan Larson felt very strongly that theatre should not just be for the elite. And in many ways, that thirty dollar live stream feels like a continuation of that mission. In fact, so much of the evening felt like such a great tribute to the legacy of RENT and Jonathan Larson. Seeing so many performers that have come through RENT and since gone on to have incredible careers. so many incredible performers have been a part of RENT at some point, and so getting to see them all, not just the original cast, step back into these roles was so special. Like, yes, don't get me wrong, I loved seeing Idina play Maureen again. But I also loved anytime we would enter the multiverse and we would see, like, four different couples singing Take Me or Leave Me, or five different marks singing Halloween. Those I thought were some of the coolest moments, and also something that separates this anniversary concert from a lot of previous ones. And could they have picked a more perfect venue than the Richard Rodgers Theatre, where Hamilton is currently playing? a show that very much is blazing the trail That rent helped to pave. It felt like this beautiful full circle moment, and how cool that we got to experience it from the comfort of our own homes.
